approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would authorise spending from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for government services that are not part of its ordinary annual operations.
It would provide the final seven-twelfths of estimated annual appropriations for the 2025-26 financial year, covering government expenditure from December 2025 to June 2026.
The bill includes direct funding for two new federal bodies: the Defence and Veterans’ Services Commission and the Australian Naval Nuclear Power Safety Regulator.
Authorises spending for non-ordinary annual government services.
Provides the remaining seven-twelfths of annual appropriations for 2025-26.
Funds two new non-corporate Commonwealth entities.
Reflects government decisions, election commitments, and savings measures.
Updates appropriation numbers from the lapsed bills to reflect current estimates.
The federal government and its agencies, including two new entities: the Defence and Veterans’ Services Commission and the Australian Naval Nuclear Power Safety Regulator.

Moved the appropriation bills for 2025-26, reporting that they would provide the remaining seven-twelfths of annual appropriations and fund budget measures, with approximately $83.4 billion sought from the Consolidated Revenue Fund and a $216.2 million reduction from the lapsed bills.

Supported the appropriation bills to ensure continuity of government services but argued that the government's economic management had weakened living standards, increased spending, debt and taxes, and failed to grow productivity; he called for fiscal rules to contain spending.

Declared that Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026, Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2025-2026 and Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026 stood referred to the Federation Chamber for further debate.
Returned Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026, Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2025-2026 and Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2025-2026 to the House for further consideration.

Moved to suspend standing and sessional orders to set expedited proceedings and portfolio timeframes for the appropriation bills, require questions to be put without debate at specified stages, and allow variations only on a motion moved by a Minister.
